title.en: Saving Zhao with No Clean Option

dek.zh: 秦军围住邯郸，魏王派出去的十万大军停在边境上不许前进；公子无忌手里没有兵，只有一群门客，和一个不得不做的决定。
dek.en: Qin's army has the Zhao capital of Handan surrounded, and the hundred thousand troops the king of Wei sent to relieve it have been halted at the frontier and told to hold. Prince Wuji has no army, only a band of retainers, and a decision he cannot get out of.

heading.en: A Turn at the East Gate

paras.zh: 魏安釐王二十年，魏公子无忌带着百余乘车骑出了大梁城，准备去秦军阵前拼命，与赵国同归于尽。车过城东的夷门，他停下来见侯嬴，把这打算原原本本告诉了他。侯嬴只送了一句「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」。车队走出几里，《史记》写无忌「心不快」；他掉转车头，回来问侯嬴。
paras.en: In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, Prince Wuji rode out of the city of Daliang with a hundred-odd chariots and horsemen, intending to hurl himself at the Qin army and die alongside the state of Zhao. Passing the Yimen, the eastern gate of the city, he stopped to see Hou Ying, an old gatekeeper he trusted, and told him the plan outright. Hou Ying saw him off with a single line — "Push on, my lord; I am old and cannot follow you". The column had gone a few li when the Records of the Grand Historian has Wuji "troubled in his heart"; he turned the chariots around and came back to ask Hou Ying what he had missed.

paras.zh: 难处摆在那里：秦军围住赵都邯郸，魏王已经派将军晋鄙率十万大军救赵，却传令止步，把军队留在邺观望。无忌几次请求魏王发兵，又让门客辩士轮番劝说，魏王怕秦，始终不听。他手里只剩下百余乘车骑和一群门客。去是送死；不去，邯郸旦暮可下，而他的姐姐就在城里。
paras.en: The difficulty was plain to see. Qin forces had invested Handan, the Zhao capital. King Anxi had already sent General Jin Pi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao, then ordered him to halt and camp at Ye and watch. Wuji had petitioned the king again and again, and set every persuasive talker in his household on the case; the king feared Qin and would not budge. What Wuji had left were a hundred-odd chariots and a band of retainers. Riding out meant dying for nothing. Staying meant Handan could fall any day — and his own sister was inside the walls.

heading.en: A Relief Army That Stopped Halfway

paras.zh: 魏安釐王二十年，秦昭王在破赵长平军之后，进兵围邯郸。无忌的姐姐是平原君夫人，她几次写信给魏王和无忌求救。魏王于是派将军晋鄙将十万众救赵。
paras.en: In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, King Zhao of Qin, having destroyed Zhao's army at Changping, marched on and laid siege to Handan. Wuji's sister was the wife of Lord Pingyuan. She wrote letter after letter to the King of Wei and to Wuji begging for help, and the king sent General Jin Pi with a hundred thousand troops to rescue Zhao.

paras.zh: 秦王派使者告诉魏王，把话挑明：邯郸旦夕可下，诸侯谁敢来救，等打下赵国，就移兵先打谁。魏王怕了，派人止住晋鄙，让大军驻在邺，「名為救趙，實持兩端以觀望」——名义上救赵，实际是两边看风向。
paras.en: Qin's envoy put the matter bluntly to the king of Wei: Handan would fall within days, and whichever of the other states dared to come to Zhao's relief, Qin would turn on it first once Zhao was finished. The king was frightened. He sent men to stop Jin Pi and had the great army camp at Ye — "in name a rescue of Zhao, in fact holding both sides and waiting to see which way things broke."

paras.zh: 平原君的使者一批接一批赶到魏国，冠盖相属，话也越说越重：我高攀这门婚姻，是以为公子高义、能急人之困；如今邯郸旦暮降秦而魏国救兵不至，这份高义在哪里？哪怕你看不起我赵胜，独不怜公子姊邪——难道连你的姐姐也不可怜吗？
paras.en: Lord Pingyuan's envoys now arrived in Wei in an unbroken stream, official carriages crowding the road, and their reproaches grew sharper with every trip. I attached myself to this marriage, one of them said on his master's behalf, because I took the prince for a man of high principle, one who hurries to relieve another's distress. Now Handan may surrender to Qin any day and Wei's rescue has not come — where is that principle? "Even if you think little of me, Zhao Sheng, have you no pity for your own sister?"

paras.zh: 无忌几次请求魏王，宾客辩士说王万端，魏王畏秦，终不听。无忌自度无法从魏王那里得到兵，「計不獨生而令趙亡」——不能自己活着而让赵国灭亡，于是约集宾客，备好百余乘车骑，打算带门客去拼死。这就是他出城那天的打算。
paras.en: Wuji petitioned the king several times, and his retainers, debaters and persuaders alike, argued the case from every angle. King Anxi feared Qin and never relented. Wuji judged that he would never get troops out of the king, and decided he would not "live on alone and let Zhao perish." So he gathered his retainers, readied a hundred-odd chariots, and meant to lead his men into the Qin lines to die with Zhao. That was the plan he rode out with.

paras.zh: 无忌平日「仁而下士」，不论贤与不肖都谦恭礼交，不敢以富贵骄人，方圆几千里的人争相投奔，门下食客三千人。有一次他与魏王下棋，北方边境举烽火报警，说赵寇将入界。魏王放下棋要召大臣商议，无忌说是赵王打猎；不久传话回来，果然如此。他说是门客能探得赵王的私事。《史记》写，此后魏王「畏公子之賢能，不敢任公子以國政」。
paras.en: Wuji's reputation rested on his habit of humbling himself before men of talent: humane and courteous to scholars whether able or not, never letting wealth and rank make him proud. Men competed to join him from a country several thousand li around, and three thousand retainers ate at his gate. Once, while he and the king were playing a board game, beacons flared on the northern frontier: "Zhao raiders are crossing the border." The king put down the game and wanted to summon his ministers. Wuji said it was merely the king of Zhao out hunting, not a raid. Before long word came from the north that it had indeed been a hunt. A retainer of mine, Wuji said, has a way of learning the king of Zhao's private business and reports it to me. From then on, the Records says, the king "dreaded the prince's ability, and did not dare entrust him with affairs of state."

paras.zh: 门客里有一位侯嬴，年七十，家贫，在大梁夷门守门。无忌想厚赠他，他不肯收，说自己修身絜行几十年，终不能因为守门穷困而受财。无忌于是置酒大会宾客，空出车上左边的尊位，亲自去迎侯嬴。侯嬴穿着破旧衣冠，径直登上上座，也不谦让，为的是看无忌的反应；无忌执辔，愈恭。侯嬴又在集市上故意站了很久，让过路人都来围观；无忌的脸色始终不变。到家后无忌请他坐上座，向在座宾客一一介绍，宾客皆惊。侯嬴后来自己说破：他这样做是想成全公子礼贤下士的名声；市人因此把他看作小人，称无忌是能下士的长者。宴罢，侯嬴成为上客。
paras.en: Among the retainers was Hou Ying, seventy years old and poor, a gatekeeper at the Yimen. Wuji sought him out and tried to present him with a handsome gift. Hou Ying would not take it: he had kept himself and his conduct clean for decades, he said, and would not accept the prince's money simply because gatekeeping left him poor. So Wuji laid on a feast for all his retainers, and once the guests were seated, he went out with his carriage and escort, left the seat of honor on the left of the chariot empty, and fetched Hou Ying himself. Hou Ying, in his shabby robe and cap, climbed straight up into that seat without a word of demur — a test of Wuji, this was — and Wuji took the reins and grew only more respectful. Hou Ying then stood about a long time in the marketplace so that passers-by would stare; Wuji's manner never changed. At the house Wuji showed Hou Ying to the seat of honor and presented him to the assembled guests one by one, and the guests were astonished. Hou Ying later spelled out his reasoning: he was a mere gatekeeper, and the prince had personally come for him before a crowd. "I wanted to make your name," he said, "so I stood a long time by your carriage in the market while people watched, and the more I tried you, the more respectful you became. The townsfolk took me for a lout and you for a true elder who can humble himself before scholars." When the feast broke up, Hou Ying became Wuji's chief retainer.

heading.en: The Tiger Tally, the Iron Mace, and Eighty Thousand Men

paras.zh: 折回夷门之后，侯嬴说出真正的办法。晋鄙的兵符平时收在魏王卧室内；如姬最得魏王宠爱，出入卧内，有能力偷出来。侯嬴说，如姬的父亲被人所杀，她为此出资三年，从魏王以下都想替她报父仇而未能；如姬向无忌哭诉，无忌派门客斩了仇人的头献给她。侯嬴的判断是：如姬愿为公子死，只是没有机会；公子一开口，她必答应。得虎符，夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。
paras.en: Back at the Yimen, Hou Ying laid out the one plan that could work. The command tally that authenticated orders to Jin Pi's army — matched half to half, one side held by the general, one by the king — was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber. Lady Ru, the king's favorite, came and went in the bedchamber freely and could steal it out. Hou Ying spelled out why she would. Her father had been murdered; for three years she had put up money to see her father's death avenged, and no one, the king included, had been able to bring it off. She had wept to Wuji, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and present it to her. Hou Ying's judgment was that Lady Ru would gladly die for Wuji and had simply never had the chance to serve him; one word from the prince and she would agree. Get the tally, take over Jin Pi's army, go north to rescue Zhao and push Qin back from the west — "an achievement worthy of the Five Hegemons."

paras.zh: 无忌照计行事，向如姬开口。如姬果然盗出晋鄙的兵符，交给了他。
paras.en: Wuji followed the plan and asked Lady Ru. She did steal Jin Pi's tally and give it to him.

paras.zh: 侯嬴接着提醒他最危险的一步。「將在外，主令有所不受」——即便兵符合上，晋鄙也可能不交兵权，再向魏王请示，事情就危险了。他让无忌带上屠者朱亥同行：晋鄙听从，最好；不听，让朱亥动手。
paras.en: Hou Ying then warned him about the step that could ruin everything. "A general in the field need not obey every command from his sovereign." Even if the tally matched, Jin Pi might refuse to hand over the army and send to the king instead, and then the whole thing was in danger. Hou Ying told him to take the butcher Zhu Hai along: if Jin Pi complied, well and good; if he did not, Zhu Hai could strike.

paras.zh: 无忌听了流泪，说晋鄙是「嚄唶宿將」，此去恐怕不听，那就必然要杀他，「是以泣耳，豈畏死哉」。朱亥是侯嬴早先推荐的屠者，隐于市井；无忌几次登门，朱亥不回谢，无忌当时还觉得奇怪。
paras.en: Wuji wept at that. Jin Pi was an old campaigner of the shouting, veteran stamp, he said, and would, he feared, refuse — in which case he would have to be killed. "That is why I weep — do you think I fear death?" Zhu Hai was the butcher Hou Ying had recommended earlier, a man of worth hidden in the marketplace. Wuji had called on him several times, and Zhu Hai had never once returned the courtesy, which Wuji had found odd at the time.

paras.zh: 这次朱亥答得干脆：我是市井里操刀的屠户，公子几次来问候我，我不回谢，是以为小礼无用；如今公子有急，正是我效命的时候。侯嬴则说自己年老不能随行，请让他算着无忌的行程，在无忌抵达晋鄙军中的那天，北向自刭相送。《史记》记，后来侯嬴果然「北鄉自剄」。
paras.en: This time Zhu Hai answered without hesitation: "I am a knife-wielding butcher in the market. You have come to see me in person again and again, and I never answered in kind because small courtesies are of no use. Now that you are in a fix, this is the moment for me to give my life." Hou Ying, for his part, said he was too old to go. Let him reckon the days of Wuji's journey, he asked, and on the day Wuji reached Jin Pi's army he would cut his own throat facing north, to see him off. The Records later confirms that Hou Ying did cut his throat facing north.

paras.zh: 无忌到邺，假传魏王令来代晋鄙。晋鄙合了符，仍有疑心，举手看着他说：我如今拥十万之众屯在边境，是国家重任，一辆车来接替我，是怎么回事？打算不听。朱亥从袖中抽出四十斤铁椎，椎杀晋鄙。无忌于是接管军队，下令：父子都在军中的，父亲回家；兄弟都在军中的，兄长回家；独子没有兄弟的，回去奉养父母。选出八万人，进兵击秦军。
paras.en: At Ye, Wuji declared that he was replacing Jin Pi by the king's order. Jin Pi matched the two halves of the tally and was still suspicious. He raised his hand and looked hard at Wuji: "I hold a hundred thousand men on the frontier, a grave charge for the state, and now a single carriage comes to relieve me. What is the meaning of this?" He was on the point of refusing. Zhu Hai drew from his sleeve an iron mace weighing forty catties and killed him. Wuji took over the army and gave orders in the camp: fathers and sons both serving, the father goes home; brothers both serving, the elder brother goes home; an only son with no brothers goes home to care for his parents. From the men left he picked eighty thousand, and advanced on the Qin army.

paras.zh: 秦军解围退走，邯郸得存。赵王和平原君亲自到边界迎接，平原君背着箭袋在前面引路；赵王再拜，说自古贤人没有赶得上公子的。
paras.en: The Qin army raised the siege and drew off; Handan was saved and Zhao preserved. The king of Zhao and Lord Pingyuan came out to the border to meet Wuji in person, Lord Pingyuan with a quiver of arrows on his back, leading the way. The king of Zhao bowed twice and said that no worthier man had appeared since antiquity.

paras.zh: 赵孝成王感激他矫令夺兵而存赵，与平原君商量，要拿五座城封给他。无忌听说，「意驕矜而有自功之色」。一位门客劝他：别人对你有德，不可忘；你对别人有德，最好忘掉。矫魏王令、夺晋鄙兵，「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」，还自骄自功，我私下以为不可取。无忌「立自責，似若無所容者」。后来赵王以主人之礼相迎，无忌侧身辞让，自言有罪过，「以負於魏，無功於趙」。赵王因他一再辞让，口不忍献五城，最后把鄗给他作汤沐邑，魏国也把信陵还给他。
paras.en: King Xiaocheng of Zhao, grateful that Wuji had seized the army on a forged order and saved Zhao, took counsel with Lord Pingyuan and proposed to enfeoff him with five cities. When Wuji heard, he "showed a self-satisfied look, as if the credit were his own." A retainer came to him: kindness done to you must never be forgotten, he said; kindness you do to another is best forgotten. Taking the tally and Jin Pi's army on your own authority — "toward Zhao you have done a service; toward Wei you cannot be called a loyal minister." To go on preening yourself over it is something I cannot approve. Wuji "at once blamed himself, as if there were nowhere he could hide." Later, when the king of Zhao received him with the rites of a host, Wuji stood to the side, declined the honor, and pronounced himself at fault: "I have failed Wei and done nothing for Zhao." Because he kept declining, the king of Zhao could not bring himself to hand over the five cities. In the end the king gave him the town of Hao to support his household, and Wei restored to him the city of Xinling.

paras.zh: 魏王对他盗兵符、矫杀晋鄙，是发怒的，无忌自己也清楚。秦军退去之后，他让将领把魏军带回魏国，自己与门客留在赵国。后来他自己回顾此事，说「始吾聞平原君賢，故負魏王而救趙」——当初以为平原君贤明，才辜负魏王去救赵。
paras.en: The king of Wei was angry over the stolen tally and the killing of Jin Pi, and Wuji knew it. Once Qin had been driven off and Zhao saved, he sent the Wei generals home with their troops and stayed on in Zhao with his own retainers. Looking back on it years later, he put it this way: "I first heard Lord Pingyuan was worthy, and so I failed my king of Wei to save Zhao."

paras.zh: 作者推断：把这件事读成“为朋友两肋插刀”，会错过它真正的难处。无忌的第一步不是去拼命，而是折回夷门，问侯嬴有没有别的做法。侯嬴那句「譬若以肉投餒虎，何功之有哉？尚安事客？」把勇气换成了计算：百余乘车骑投进秦军能换来什么？连门客都用不上，还要门客做什么。
paras.en: One reading: treat this as a friend staking everything for a friend and you miss where the real difficulty lay. Wuji's first move was not to charge but to turn back at the Yimen. His question to Hou Ying was whether there was another way. Hou Ying's rebuke — "it would be like throwing meat at a starving tiger. What would it accomplish? And what use would your retainers be then?" — traded courage for arithmetic: what would a hundred-odd chariots buy against the Qin army? If even his retainers could not be put to use, what were retainers for?

paras.zh: 第二步是给坏情况留人手。动手之前他已经知道，兵符再真，晋鄙也可能不交兵权（SJ0771-E17）；他也预见到这一步要杀本国的老将，所以先流泪说破（SJ0771-E18）。作者推断：把代价先讲明，事到临头就不是意外，而是执行——这并不等于代价变小了。
paras.en: Second, he staffed for the bad case before he acted. He knew going in that even a genuine tally might be refused, and Jin Pi might simply refer back to the king; he also foresaw that this step would mean killing an old general of his own state, which is why he wept and said so out loud first. The author's inference: naming the cost in advance does not make it smaller. It turns a shock into an execution of a decision already made.

paras.zh: 第三步是事成之后怎么记账。赵要封五城，门客提醒他对魏算不得忠臣，他立刻自责（SJ0771-E24）；在赵王面前自言负魏、无功于赵（SJ0771-E31）；留赵期间还说自己负魏王而救赵。作者推断：从这些言行看，这笔债他没有抹掉，军队送回魏国，自己留在赵国。不过原文也写，他留赵十年不归；魏王遣使来请，他怕魏王发怒，还禁止门下为魏使通报，留赵未必就是认下这笔债。
paras.en: Third, he kept the books honestly after it worked. Zhao was about to grant five cities; a retainer reminded him that he could not count as a loyal minister to Wei, and he blamed himself on the spot. Before the king of Zhao he declared he had failed Wei and done nothing for Zhao. While he was staying in Zhao he still said he had failed his king to save Zhao. On this reading he did not write the debt off: the army went home to Wei, and he stayed in Zhao. But the record also says he stayed in Zhao ten years without returning; when the king of Wei sent men to fetch him, he feared the king's anger and even barred his household from admitting the king's envoys, so staying there need not count as settling the debt.

paras.zh: 作者设想的另一种做法：只递证据、不动自己的位置。但平原君已经说邯郸旦暮降秦（SJ0771-E11），拖下去的代价由城里的人承担。作者推断：他选的不是一个干净的选项，而是当时能改变局面的一种做法，代价是杀本国将军、失信于魏王。
paras.en: The alternative the author imagines: simply passing the evidence up the chain and leaving his own position untouched. But Lord Pingyuan had already said that Handan might surrender to Qin any day, and the price of holding back would be paid by the people inside the walls. On this reading, what Wuji chose was not a clean option; it was one that could change the situation, at the price of killing his own general and losing the trust of his king.

paras.zh: 司马迁怎么看待此事？太史公说自己过大梁，特意去寻夷门，又说信陵君结交岩穴隐者、不耻下交，「名冠諸侯，不虛耳」；褒扬落在他敬重侯嬴这一端，而不在矫令杀将上（SJ0771-E37）。代价也没有就此结束：无忌留赵十年，后来秦攻魏，毛公、薛公劝他，诸侯之所以敬重他，「徒以有魏也」，他立刻归国为将，率五国之兵破秦（SJ0771-E32、SJ0771-E34）；秦用重金收买晋鄙的门客毁谤他，魏王果然派人代将，他谢病饮酒，四年后病酒而死（SJ0771-E33）。他死后秦攻魏，拔二十城，此后十八年，秦国俘虏了魏王（SJ0771-E35）。一种解释是，这段收尾把无忌的存亡与魏国的存亡写在了一起。
paras.en: What did Sima Qian make of it? The Grand Historian writes that he passed through Daliang and made a point of finding the Yimen, and adds that Xinling's readiness to seek out recluses in mountain caves and to befriend men beneath him was something he had real cause for: "his name stood first among the lords — no empty fame." The praise lands on the end where he honored Hou Ying, not on the forged order and the slain general. And the costs did not stop there. Wuji stayed in Zhao ten years. When Qin attacked Wei, the two recluses he had befriended there — Master Mao, who lived among gamblers, and Master Xue, who hid himself among ale-sellers — told him that the only reason he was respected in Zhao and known to the lords was that he had Wei behind him; he changed countenance at once, ordered the carriage, and went back to save Wei. The king of Wei met him in tears and gave him the seal of supreme commander. Wuji called the other states to arms, led their five armies to rout Qin beyond the river, put the general Meng Ao to flight, and pursued to the Hangu Pass, after which the Qin army dared not come out. Alarmed, the king of Qin sent ten thousand jin of gold into Wei to buy off Jin Pi's former retainers, who slandered Wuji to the king: he has been an exile ten years, the lords obey only him, they want to make him king. The king heard it daily and came to believe it; he sent a replacement to take over the army. Wuji, knowing he had been pushed aside by slander a second time, excused himself on illness and spent long nights drinking with his retainers, strong wine and women, for four years, until drink killed him. After his death Qin attacked Wei, took twenty cities and set up its first commandery there, and eighteen years later captured the king of Wei and put Daliang to the sword. One reading is that this closing episode writes Wuji's survival and Wei's survival on the same line.

paras.zh: 本篇只有一个史源：《史记·魏公子列传》中的一处记述，没有第二种记载可以对勘。侯嬴献计、朱亥的答话、门客的劝谏，都是史家记述的对话，未必是逐字实录（SJ0771-E15、SJ0771-E19、SJ0771-E24）。
paras.en: This piece rests on a single source: one account in the "Biography of the Prince of Wei" in the Records of the Grand Historian, with no second version to check it against. Hou Ying's plan, Zhu Hai's reply, and the retainer's remonstrance are all speeches recorded by the historian, not necessarily verbatim transcripts.

paras.zh: 原文里的「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」是叙述用语，不是实录的心理；本文凡涉情绪处都只是转述史家的叙述。侯嬴自刭的动机、如姬盗符之后的下落，原文只写行为和一句话，没有更多交代（SJ0771-E13、SJ0771-E24、SJ0771-E20、SJ0771-E28）。
paras.en: Phrases in the original such as "troubled in his heart," "showed a self-satisfied look," and "at once blamed himself" are narrative wording, not recorded states of mind; wherever emotion enters this piece, it is only the historian's narration being relayed. Hou Ying's motive in cutting his throat, and what became of Lady Ru after she stole the tally, are given only as an act and a single line, with nothing further.

paras.zh: 「得選兵八萬人」这一数字只此一处，无旁证；晋鄙军中合符如何校验、军心如何收场，原文没有记载（SJ0771-E22、SJ0771-E29）。纪年只用原文的魏安釐王二十年，不作换算。
paras.en: The figure of "eighty thousand selected men" appears in one place only, with nothing to corroborate it; how the tally was verified at the camp and how the troops took the news are not recorded. Dates follow the original reckoning — the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei — with no conversion.

scenario.zh: 你的团队遇到明显风险，决策层因为怕一个更大的对手，把已经派出去的资源停在半路观望。你手上有第一线的证据，也有两个能干的人；推动就要绕开常规流程，还可能让自己这方吃亏。
scenario.en: Your team faces an obvious risk. Leadership, afraid of a bigger rival, has stopped already-committed resources halfway and told them to hold and watch. You have front-line evidence in hand and two capable people; pushing forward means bypassing the normal chain of command, and it may cost your own side.

question.zh: 在动手之前，你最该先问的是哪一句——这是不是拿肉投饿虎，还是对方不配合怎么办？
question.en: Before you act, which is the first question to ask: is this throwing meat at a starving tiger, or what if the person who has to comply refuses?

assumptions.zh: 决策层停手是出于对更大对手的恐惧（如秦王恫吓魏王），不是不知道风险；你有可验证的一线证据和能干的人；事情若成，功劳与对自己这方的亏欠会同时存在。
assumptions.en: Leadership stopped out of fear of a bigger rival, in the way the king of Qin's threat stopped the king of Wei — not because they failed to see the risk. You have verifiable front-line evidence and capable people. If it works, the credit and the debt to your own side will both be real.

steps.zh: 一、先把送死式的冲锋换成具体计算：手里的资源投进去能换来什么；二、动手前为“对方不配合”备好人手和止损点（侯嬴让无忌带上朱亥）；三、事成之后主动认下对自己这方的亏欠，不把功劳记在自己账上（门客劝后无忌自责）。
steps.en: First, replace the death-ride with concrete arithmetic: what would the resources at hand actually buy? Second, before acting, line up a person and a stop-loss for the case where the other party will not cooperate — Hou Ying had Wuji bring the butcher Zhu Hai. Third, after it works, put the debt to your own side on your own account and do not bank the credit — as Wuji did once the retainer spoke to him.

alternative.zh: 也可以继续走流程、把证据递上去等批复，或者只做分内的事、不动自己的位置。作者提出：这两种做法保全了程序，但代价由被围的一方承担。
alternative.en: You could also stay inside the process, pass the evidence up and wait for approval, or do only your own job and leave your position untouched. The author's point: both preserve procedure, but the cost falls on the party under siege.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本篇只有一个史源，对话未必逐字；「心不快」「意骄矜」「立自责」是叙述用语而非实录心理；八万之数、合符校验、军中收场、侯嬴自刭动机与如姬后续均无更多记载；纪年只用原文，不换算公元。
uncertainty_note.en: This piece has only one source; the speeches need not be verbatim. "Troubled in his heart," "showed a self-satisfied look," and "at once blamed himself" are narrative wording, not recorded states of mind. The figure of eighty thousand, the tally-checking, the army's reaction, Hou Ying's motive, and Lady Ru's later fate have nothing further in the record. Dates follow the original and are not converted to the common era.

preheader.zh: 偷符之前，他先折回去问了看门的老头一句
preheader.en: Before stealing the tally, he turned back and asked the old gatekeeper one question
